artists.biography: Tim Bowness is a british singer/songwriter primarily known for his work as part of the band No-Man, a long-term project with Steven Wilson from Porcupine Tree.  In addition to producing several albums with No-Man, Tim has recorded with popular Italian artist Alice, experimental guitar legend David Torn, Soft Machine's Hugh Hopper, Roger Eno, German band Centrozoon, and recorded the album Flame (1994) in collaboration with Porcupine Tree/ex-Japan keyboard player Richard Barbieri.  Tim's debut solo album, My Hotel Year, was released on the One Little Indian label in 2004.

Tim Bowness.biography: Tim Bowness is a british singer/songwriter primarily known for his work as part of the band No-Man, a long-term project with Steven Wilson from Porcupine Tree.  In addition to producing several albums with No-Man, Tim has recorded with popular Italian artist Alice, experimental guitar legend David Torn, Soft Machine's Hugh Hopper, Roger Eno, German band Centrozoon, and recorded the album Flame (1994) in collaboration with Porcupine Tree/ex-Japan keyboard player Richard Barbieri.  Tim's debut solo album, My Hotel Year, was released on the One Little Indian label in 2004.

perplexity.description:
Flowers At The Scene is the fifth solo studio album by English singer-songwriter Tim Bowness, released on March 1, 2019, through Inside Out Music and Sony Music. The album is a blend of art rock and progressive pop, characterized by atmospheric textures, melodic sophistication, and introspective lyrics. Produced by Bowness alongside Steven Wilson and Brian Hulse—marking their first joint production in over a decade—the album features a diverse array of guest musicians, including Peter Hammill, Kevin Godley, Andy Partridge, Jim Matheos, and David Longdon, among others. This collaborative approach brings a rich variety of tones and moods, while the album maintains a cohesive sound that reflects both the spirit of Bowness’s earlier work with No-Man and a sense of renewal in his solo career.

Musically, Flowers At The Scene stands out for its nuanced arrangements, subtle electronic treatments, and emotionally resonant songwriting. The album’s tracks range from driving art-rock anthems to delicate, melancholic ballads, showcasing Bowness’s distinctive voice and lyrical depth. It received widespread critical acclaim, earning a Metacritic score of 78/100 and positive reviews from outlets such as PopMatters, Mojo, and Classic Pop. Commercially, the album reached No. 5 in both the UK Rock and UK Progressive charts, No. 24 in the UK Vinyl chart, and No. 65 in the Scottish albums chart, solidifying its place as one of Bowness’s most successful and well-regarded releases.
